statement: Corollary 6(a): at x∈X_i for i=1,2, φ_Q is W-smooth iff f_i is W-smooth at x.

statement: Proposition 15: a commutative square U→X, U′→X′ is a pushout along an open immersion iff it is cartesian, U′→X′ is open, its induced complement map T→T′ is an isomorphism, and every p/t:U/t→U′/t′ is final for set-valued colimits, i.e. every (u′,a′)↓(p/t) is nonempty and connected.

statement: For p/t:V_t→V′_(t′), the condition (p/t)_!1≅1 is equivalent to π_0(v′↓(p/t)) being a singleton for every v′.
repair: Ordinary pointwise left Kan-extension formula; explicit factorization proof in p158 block.
notes: “0-connected” includes nonemptiness. This is ordinary finality, not homotopy finality.

statement: Proposition 15, Corollary 1: if Q is cartesian, U′→X′ is open, q is W-smooth, W satisfies W(5), and the induced T→T′ is an isomorphism, then Q is a categorical pushout.

statement: For any cartesian square Q and any t∈X, the induced square U/t→X/t over U′/t′→X′/t′ is cartesian.
notes: No openness or smoothness hypotheses enter; the source proves this by the cube, and the commentary gives its object-and-arrow description.

statement: If q:X→X′ is W-smooth, then q/t:X/t→X′/q(t) is W-smooth and has W-aspherical strict fibres.
notes: Smoothness of the slice map follows from locality; fibre asphericity is the local lift test at t.

statement: The pullback p/t is W-smooth with W-aspherical fibres, hence a universal W-equivalence (the source calls it a trivial W-fibration).
notes: Base change preserves smoothness and the identified fibres. The modern claim is universal weak equivalence; model-category fibrations are not asserted.

statement: Under W(5), each v′↓(p/t) is connected because the strict fibre maps to it by a W-equivalence and is W-aspherical.
notes: This is exactly condition (d) of Proposition 15, not an additional stronger finality theorem.

statement: Proposition 15, Corollary 2: if Q is cartesian, U′→X′ is open, q is a local isomorphism, and the induced complement map T→T′ is an isomorphism, then Q is a pushout.
gap_or_error: The complement map is again printed T′→T.
repair: Use induced T→T′. Since q/t and its pullback p/t are isomorphisms, Proposition 15(d) follows without any W.
notes: The direct argument is independent of the W_∞ or W_0 reductions mentioned first.

statement: If p/t is an isomorphism, every v′↓(U/t) is isomorphic to v′↓(U′/t′) and has an initial object.
notes: Hence it is nonempty and connected, proving ordinary finality.

statement: A square of presheaves is cocartesian iff its evaluation at each x∈X is a pushout of sets.
notes: Standard pointwise computation of presheaf colimits.

statement: A pushout square of sets along an injection is also a pullback and its opposite horizontal map is injective.
repair: The explicit decomposition G′(x)=F′(x)∐(G(x)\F(x)) proves both assertions; p167 commentary.

statement: A pushout square of presheaves along a monomorphism is also cartesian.
notes: Pointwise set result; the opposite horizontal map is also a monomorphism, explicit in Theorem 5.

statement: φ_X(F)=X/F, with objects (x,a), a∈F(x), and arrows u:(x,a)→(y,b) satisfying F(u)b=a, is the category-of-elements functor, naturally valued in Cat/X.
notes: The source writes the definition using arrows from representables to F.

statement: φ_X:Xhat→Cat/X is fully faithful, and its essential image consists exactly of discrete Grothendieck fibrations, equivalently local isomorphisms to X.
notes: Recalled standard equivalence, not proved anew in the manuscript.

statement: Every functor over X between two discrete fibrations over X is itself a local isomorphism.
notes: For an object, both slice projections identify canonically with X/x, and the induced slice functor is their unique comparison.

statement: The full subcategory of discrete fibrations over X is closed under pullbacks in Cat/X; these pullbacks are also pullbacks of the total categories.
notes: A pullback of a local isomorphism is a local isomorphism; compose with the structure map to X.

statement: Lemma 1: the subcategory of discrete fibrations over X is closed under finite limits in Cat/X, and φ_X preserves finite limits, hence pullback squares.
notes: Later strengthened to all small limits and colimits; p164 commentary proves the stronger known result by the degreewise nerve formula.

statement: φ_X sends presheaf monomorphisms to monomorphisms in Cat/X.
notes: Follows from finite-limit preservation, or directly from objectwise injectivity.

statement: Lemma 2: a functor which is both a monomorphism and a local isomorphism is an open immersion, and every open immersion has these two properties.
repair: Unique lifting through the slice isomorphisms proves full faithfulness and the sieve property; the converse follows by restricting slices.
notes: Monomorphism means monomorphism of the ordinary category Cat, hence injective on objects and faithful; local-isomorphism property supplies fullness.

statement: Monomorphisms between discrete fibrations over X are exactly open immersions; thus φ_X sends monomorphisms of presheaves to open immersions.
notes: Combine the previous two statements.

statement: The square of categories of elements induced by a presheaf pushout along a monomorphism is cartesian.
notes: The presheaf square is cartesian and φ_X is left exact.

statement: To prove this category-of-elements square is cocartesian, it is enough to prove that the induced functor on complementary closed subcategories is an isomorphism.
notes: Apply Proposition 15, Corollary 2; the vertical map is a local isomorphism.

statement: After the notation swap, T consists of (x,a) with a∈G(x)\F(x), and T′ consists of (x,a′) with a′∈G′(x)\F′(x). The functor T→T′ is induced by q.
